notes: Scan 014 is a portrait manuscript page with a dark authorial 4 at the head and a thin pale 13 at the bottom left. The latter is retained as external foliation. No date is written on the page.

The page lists conditions a), b), and c), each ending est épi. They concern the written image of the final object, a binary product, and a fibre product. Condition c) includes a two-level diagram with alpha and beta above alpha0 and both arrows directed toward alpha0. The subsequent prose discusses the case where phi! is left exact and writes a morphism f from the calligraphic topos symbol to A-hat and the equality phi!=f*. This is an account of what the author writes, not an independently asserted proof.

The lower prose says that the indicated arrows are then isomorphisms, voices a converse, and immediately refers to the canonical-colimit expression F=varinjlim over A/F of alpha. It ends with an unfinished revised phrase On voit ... de la = façon pour b) et c). No continuation beyond this sheet has been supplied.

The original page, exactly two overlapping native-resolution halves, and ten crops were actually viewed. Crop p06 initially clipped the upper strokes of the disputed word after essentiellement. Before deciding that place, p10 was made with full-height margin and viewed. This was correction of an initially incomplete crop, not reinspection of a decided reading. No OCR, outside research, or TeX compilation was used.

The 25 reading units count the author and external pagination, both levels of the diagram, the colimit’s separate A/F baseline, and the two baselines of the final revision. All physical writing blocks and separate alterations are inventoried.

The two calligraphic X forms, in item a) and in the morphism display, show the two bowed crossing curves and horizontal bar of the supplied current notation table. The exclamation subscript on phi is confirmed by its separate lower dot throughout this sheet. No lower exclamation has been regularized to 1.

The cancellation after correspond is opaque. Its proposed à remains inherited and explicitly doubtful; the following live à is clear. In the final revision, Mais is readable, while the connecting strokes in peut-on avoir remain doubtful under the strike. The scope and attachment of de la = façon pour are clear independently of those deleted letters.

The word after essentiellement is unaccented evident or abbreviated evid-t, supported by the low initial loop, internal i-dot, and tall looped d. There is no detached accent over the initial e. This is a local spelling reading, not a general decision that the author omits accents.

After the colimit formula, a point–wavering stroke–point sequence is visible but not securely identified. The separate low dark mark before On voit may be punctuation or a non-textual blot; its period reading is retained only with a new doubt. Pale gray blemishes above the leftmost F and below pour on the preceding line are not transcribed as punctuation.

H’s explicit author-page note, its historical revision comment, its bottom explanatory note, and the introductory transition les conditions : are excluded from correction counts and source transcription. Their exclusion is recorded in difference_coverage; the bottom foliation 13 is counted separately as an actual H omission.

The author’s qualification is literally “je présume que l’inverse est vrai également,” followed by “Oui -- et c’est essentiellement evident [ending now doubtful].” The reader preserves both stages of that self-check, without asserting a proof of the converse. Condition a) explicitly concerns the terminal object e of the presheaf category; it is the nontrivial condition relevant to the singleton-index anomaly recorded at scan015.

Independent audit: the ending of the word after essentiellement is now doubtful between evident and evid-t, with no initial accent in either reading. The below-line revision reads pour b) et c), supported by the initial p and terminal r. The small post-colimit sequence and the separate possible punctuation blot remain unresolved.
